resume_author: "One doesn't have to operate with great malice to do great harm. The absence of empathy and understanding are sufficient".
text_post: It's not such a crazy notion, I have a friend who firmly believes marriage should be a formal written contract mandatorily renewable ten yearly, and before you get a house or a kid or a dog. His belief is that the state should not impose one-size-fits-all contract terms with the uncertainty of the courts determining how they apply in individual circumstances. He believes that like any business the state should determine minimum standards and let individuals negotiate their individual conditions. Essentially it's a concept of the enforceable mandatory prenup, but as frequently updated as you'd update your life and house insurance.  And now I've largely lost my romantic notion of two hearts joining forever and see it more like a business venture, I think he's right. It would save a lot of problems if we were negotiating terms at the beginning and throughout as two equal [business] partners of life, rather than leaving it until the end when the partnerships broken down and it's a cash grab for what you're "owed". Anon, I don't think that divorce invalidates marriage, but I do think it makes us view marriage very differently, I hope.
